To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) trading systems can be trained by optimizing the Sharpe ratio or differential Sharpe ratio and that this leads to better performance than training by optimizing profit or by using forecasts, (2) portfolio management systems can be trained to optimize the Sharpe ratio, differential Sharpe ratio or utility and that this leads, in general, to better performance than profit maximization, and (3) there is evidence for out-of-sample predictablity in the stock market for the S&P 500
reinforcement learning methods that optimize the differential Sharpe performance function yield better trading and portfolio management results than those that maximize profits.

reinforcement learning can be used to optimize trading systems and portfolio management systems and that the Sharpe ratio, when properly adjusted, is an effective measure of performance for such systems.

the application of reinforcement learning to trading and portfolio management.
